jobs.title: Director of Operations and Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
Purpose of the Position

The Director of Operations and Strategic Partnerships (Director) strengthens organizational effectiveness by ensuring that core operations run with rigor, consistency and efficiency while building and managing strategic partnerships that advance the organization’s mission and reach. 

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director owns the day-to-day execution and continuous improvement of core operational systems – including contracting, onboarding and offboarding, technology, office operations and administrative processes – and coordinates closely with external legal, accounting and other professional partners.

The Director also leads the organization’s strategic partnerships function end-to-end: refining and executing partnership strategy, identifying and prioritizing prospective partners, developing and managing relationships, creating strategic plans for each partnership and executing those plans in concert with strategic partners, structuring collaborations and measuring partnership performance. Working closely with the Executive Director, Founder and Chairman, Senior Product Manager and other team members, the Director ensures partnerships translate organizational priorities into meaningful opportunities for targeted distribution, audience reach and engagement, learning and co-creation, and measurable short-, intermediate- and long-term impact.

As a senior member of the team, the Director also manages the Director of Convenings and Senior Product Manager, providing strategic guidance, setting clear expectations and ensuring strong coordination across partnerships, convenings, products and launches. The Director enables these functional leaders to operate successfully while ensuring priorities remain aligned, dependencies are managed and issues requiring executive judgment are elevated appropriately.

The ideal candidate combines operational excellence with relationship-building and strategic execution. This individual will be
equally comfortable improving an internal process, managing a complex agreement, building a partnership pipeline, mapping and measuring inputs, activities, outputs and outcomes and representing the organization with sophisticated external stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Operations & Systems

Oversee the day-to-day execution of core operational processes, ensuring systems are efficient, reliable, well-documented and consistently implemented.
Maintain, improve and develop standard operating procedures (SOPs), workflows, templates and other systems that strengthen organizational efficiency, clarity and accountability.
Identify operational gaps, bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement and proactively design solutions that enable the organization to operate effectively as it grows.
Partner with the Executive Director to translate operational priorities into clear plans, owners, timelines and follow-through.

Contracting, Legal & Vendor Administration

Own the administration and execution of approved contracts and agreements.
Manage contracting workflows from approved requests through drafting/template preparation, review, signature, filing and tracking, ensuring agreements move efficiently and required documentation is complete.
Coordinate with outside legal counsel on contract review and other approved legal matters, escalating substantive questions and decisions to the Executive Director as appropriate.
Administer DocuSign and related contract-management systems and maintain accurate, organized records of executed agreements, renewal dates and relevant obligations.
Coordinate operationally with vendors and professional-services providers and ensure required administrative processes are completed accurately and on time.
Partner with the Senior Product Manager and other internal owners on vendor engagements, with the Director owning contracting and administrative mechanics while substantive work, deliverables and performance remain with the relevant functional owner.

People Operations & Onboarding

Administer established people-operations processes, including employee, intern and contractor onboarding and offboarding, required documentation, personnel records and related workflows.
Ensure new team members receive the technology, agreements, materials, access and operational support required to begin work effectively.
Maintain and continuously improve onboarding, offboarding and other personnel-related SOPs in partnership with the Executive Director and external advisers as appropriate.
Support approved hiring and contractor processes by coordinating operational requirements and documentation.
Escalate questions involving compensation, performance management, employee policy or other substantive people decisions to the Executive Director.

Technology, Office & Administrative Infrastructure

Oversee day-to-day technology administration, including equipment procurement and deployment, account/access coordination, technology requests and troubleshooting with external IT partners.
Manage office and workplace operations to ensure team members have the physical and digital infrastructure necessary to perform effectively.
Maintain relevant inventories, trackers and operational records and anticipate upcoming organizational needs.
Coordinate with external providers to resolve technology and workplace issues efficiently and proactively.

Strategic Partnerships Strategy & Execution

Lead and continuously refine our strategic partnerships strategy in alignment with organizational priorities, target audiences and desired outcomes.
Develop and maintain a disciplined partnership pipeline, including researching, identifying, segmenting and prioritizing prospective organizations and relationships.
Translate organizational and programmatic priorities into clear partnership opportunities and specific external asks.
Proactively conduct outreach, cultivate relationships and move prospective partnerships from initial conversation through defined collaboration.
Structure and negotiate collaborations in partnership with the Executive Director, Founder/Chairman and other relevant internal stakeholders.
Develop partnership plans that clarify the strategic rationale, desired outcomes, roles, next steps, owners and measures of success for priority relationships.
Manage ongoing partner relationships with consistency and professionalism, ensuring commitments are fulfilled and opportunities for deeper collaboration are identified.
Establish systems for tracking partnership activity, relationship health, outcomes and organizational value and use those insights to refine partnership strategy over time.

External Representation and Relationship Management

Independently manage strategic partner relationships while ensuring the Executive Director and Founder are engaged at the appropriate moments in senior or principal-level relationships.
Prepare the Executive Director and Founder for priority external engagements by synthesizing relationship context, strategic objectives, open questions and recommended next steps.
Over time, represent the organization at selected external meetings, convenings and events as appropriate.
Exercise excellent judgment regarding when to independently advance a relationship and when to elevate decisions or opportunities to organizational leadership.

Cross-Functional Partnership with Product

Manage and partner closely with the Senior Product Manager to translate IoG’s product portfolio and launch priorities into actionable partnership and distribution strategies.
Own the institutional relationship, while the Senior Product Manager owns the product and launch strategy: Product defines the audiences, distribution needs, activation requirements and timing for a launch; the Director develops and manages the relationships necessary to deliver against those needs.
Jointly develop launch distribution plans that identify priority partners, specific partnership asks, timing, responsibilities and expected reach or impact.
Ensure partner commitments are translated into concrete actions and coordinated with internal launch plans and timelines.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Management

Manage and develop the Director of Convenings and Senior Product Manager, establishing clear priorities, expectations and accountability while empowering each leader to own their respective function.
Partner closely with the Director of Convenings on institutional relationships connected to the Generosity Symposium, Generosity Salons and other convenings. The Director of Operations & Strategic Partnerships remains the institutional relationship owner, while the Director of Convenings owns the convening-specific collaboration, strategy, experience and execution.
Ensure effective coordination across partnerships, convenings and products, proactively identifying dependencies, resolving cross-functional issues and maintaining clarity of ownership.
Support direct reports in translating organizational strategy into clear plans, priorities and measures of success and provide ongoing coaching, feedback and performance management.
Elevate organizational, strategic or other consequential decisions requiring Executive Director or Founder/Chairman judgment while enabling routine decisions to be made at the lowest appropriate level.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Role Description
The Executive Director is a full-time, remote position responsible for overseeing overall company strategy, operations, and growth. This role includes setting organizational goals, guiding logistics and procurement activities, and ensuring that service quality and delivery timelines are consistently met. The Executive Director will collaborate closely with operations, finance, and client service teams to manage budgets, optimize processes, and maintain strong customer relationships. Day-to-day tasks involve reviewing performance metrics, leading strategic planning, supporting business development initiatives, and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and company policies. The role also includes building and mentoring a high-performing team and representing the organization with key partners and stakeholders.
Qualifications

Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing operations, strategy, or logistics in a transportation, supply chain, or related sector.
Strong skills in strategic planning, budgeting, and performance management, with the ability to interpret data and make informed decisions.
Experience in business development, client relationship management, or partnerships that drive revenue and organizational growth.
Proficiency with digital tools and systems used for logistics, procurement, and remote team collaboration.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across diverse teams and stakeholders.
Proven ability to manage remote teams, prioritize multiple initiatives, and maintain accountability for outcomes.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or a related field; an advanced degree is an advantage.
Familiarity with regional transport routes and regulatory requirements between Dar es Salaam and Njombe is a plus.

jobs.title: Director/Managing Director, Investment Grade Syndicate
jobs.description:
Description

The Director/MD Investment Grade Syndicate is responsible for leading the syndication and execution of investment grade debt offerings, including corporate bonds, financials, and sovereigns. This role involves managing deal flow, pricing strategy, investor engagement, and regulatory compliance, while coordinating across origination, sales, trading, and legal teams. The successful candidate will be a strategic leader with deep market knowledge, strong client relationships, and a proven track record in syndicate execution.

Consistent travel to meet with issuers and investors is expected.

This position may be based in Charlotte, NC or NYC, NY.

Primary Responsibilities Include

Deal Execution & Syndication:
Lead the syndication process for investment grade debt transactions across currencies and geographies.
Oversee pricing discussions, book-building, allocation strategy, and investor targeting.
Ensure seamless coordination with issuers, legal counsel, and internal stakeholders.

Market Intelligence & Strategy:
Monitor primary and secondary market conditions to advise on optimal issuance windows and pricing.
Provide thought leadership on market trends, investor sentiment, and regulatory developments.
Contribute to strategic planning and product innovation within the debt capital markets business.

Client Coverage & Relationship Management:
Maintain and grow relationships with key issuers, institutional investors, and internal partners.
Represent the syndicate desk in client meetings, roadshows, and investor calls.
Deliver high-quality market updates and execution insights to clients and internal teams.

Team Leadership & Development:
Mentor a team of syndicate professionals, fostering a high-performance culture.
Promote collaboration across origination, sales, and trading teams.
Ensure adherence to compliance, risk, and governance standards.

Qualifications, Education, Certifications And/or Other Professional Credentials

Minimum 10 years of experience in investment grade syndicate or related capital markets roles. Experience with Structured Products is a plus, but not required.
Deep understanding of fixed income markets, investor dynamics, and regulatory frameworks.
Proven leadership and team management experience.
Strong communication, negotiation, and analytical skills.
Bachelor's degree and relevant licenses required.

Hours & Work Schedule

Hours per Week: 40+
Work Schedule: Monday to Friday

Pay Transparency

The salary range for this position is $300,000 to $400,000 per year, plus an opportunity to earn an annual discretionary bonus. Actual pay is based on various factors including but not limited to the work location, and relevant skills and experience.

We offer competitive pay, comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage, retirement benefits, maternity/paternity leave, flexible work arrangements, education reimbursement, wellness programs and more. Note, Citizens’ paid time off policy exceeds the mandatory, paid sick or paid time-away policy of very local and state jurisdiction in the United States. For an overview of our benefits, visit https://jobs.citizensbank.com/benefits.

Some job boards have started using jobseeker-reported data to estimate salary ranges for roles. If you apply and qualify for this role, a recruiter will discuss accurate pay guidance.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Citizens, its parent, subsidiaries, and related companies (Citizens) provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all colleagues and applicants for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, citizenship, physical or mental disability, perceived disability or history or record of a disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity or expression, genetic information, genetic characteristic, marital or domestic partner status, victim of domestic violence, family status/parenthood, medical condition, military or veteran status, national origin, pregnancy/childbirth/lactation, colleague’s or a dependent’s reproductive health decision making, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by federal, state and/or local laws. At Citizens, we are committed to fostering an inclusive culture that enables all colleagues to bring their best selves to work every day and everyone is expected to be treated with respect and professionalism. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, qualifications, performance and capability.

Why Work for Us

At Citizens, you'll find a customer-centric culture built around helping our customers and giving back to our local communities. When you join our team, you are part of a supportive and collaborative workforce, with access to training and tools to accelerate your potential and maximize your career growth
